title: Exclusion Statistics as a Thermodynamic Resource in Quantum Heat Engines
authors: Sampurna Karmakar, Aziz Hasan, Sourin Das
abstract: The maximum power extractable from a quantum thermoelectric heat engine operating with free fermion carriers is bounded by the universal Whitney limit, $P_{\text{fermion}}^{\max} \simeq 0.0321π^2 k_B^2(T_L-T_R)^2/h$. We demonstrate that this bound is not fundamental to quantum heat engines but is instead an artifact of fermionic statistics. Within the nonlinear Landauer-Büttiker framework, a bosonic working medium yields a strictly enhanced universal maximum power, $P_{\text{boson}}^{\max} = (\ln 2)^2\, k_B^2(T_L-T_R)^2/h$, exceeding the fermionic limit by a factor of $(\ln 2)^2/(0.0321π^2) \approx 1.52$. We propose magnon transport through a ferromagnetic spin chain as an experimentally viable bosonic realization. Incorporating Haldane fractional exclusion statistics with parameter $g$ provides a continuous interpolation between the bosonic ($g = 0$) and fermionic ($g = 1$) limits, revealing a monotonic enhancement of maximum power for $g < 1$ at reduced bias cost. These results establish quantum statistical exclusion as a previously unrecognized and independently tunable thermodynamic resource, opening performance regimes inaccessible to conventional carrier-engineering approaches.
summary: This work demonstrates that the statistical nature of charge carriers fundamentally limits the maximum power achievable by quantum heat engines. By modeling magnon transport and incorporating Haldane's fractional exclusion statistics, the authors show that bosonic behavior significantly enhances this limit over fermionic predictions, establishing statistical exclusion as a tunable thermodynamic resource.
main_problem: To investigate quantum statistical exclusion as a thermodynamic resource by comparing the maximum power extractable from heat engines operating with different carrier statistics (fermionic vs. bosonic).
main_result: Bosonic working media yield strictly enhanced universal maximum power compared to fermionic limits, and Haldane's fractional statistics parameterizes this enhancement continuously.
method: The analysis uses the nonlinear Landauer-Büttiker framework applied to a quantum thermoelectric heat engine model.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using magnon transport through a ferromagnetic spin chain, analyzed via an effective quadratic bosonic tight-binding Hamiltonian in the low-temperature limit.
key_observables: Maximum power ($P_{	ext{max}}$), efficiency ($\eta$), and the ratio of maximum power output vs. fermionic bound.
important_parameters: Haldane exclusion statistics parameter ($g$), temperature difference ($T_L - T_R$), and magnetic field strengths defining chemical potentials.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the nonlinear Landauer-Büttiker framework, assuming low temperatures for noninteracting magnon approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the spin chain setup, transmission profiles showing filtering thresholds, and plots comparing power output ratios versus the statistics parameter g.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical bounds using Landauer-Büttiker formalism, compares fermionic vs. bosonic limits, introduces Haldane interpolation, and applies this framework to a magnon transport model to quantify the enhancement.
why_interesting: It connects fundamental concepts of quantum statistics (bosonic/fermionic nature) directly to macroscopic thermodynamic performance metrics like power output in mesoscopic devices.
